body:
With NX8's 8-bit static formats, the tensor that loses most even in its best format is layernorm bias in openai-community/gpt2: 34.5 dB SQNR (signal-to-quantization-noise ratio; higher is better) in fp8_e3m4, measured on that tensor alone by the format search. Measured on 6 models with a format search (of 277 surveyed).

Model outputs keep a median 24.3 dB SQNR against full precision, the worst 12.7 dB (stable-diffusion-v1-5/stable-diffusion-v1-5:vae). 4 of 6 models with a prediction metric (top-1, perplexity or agreement) lose some of it; the most: stable-diffusion-v1-5/stable-diffusion-v1-5:vae (token agreement 100% → 68%: the share of token positions whose predicted token matches full precision's), openai-community/gpt2 (perplexity 47 → 52.5, higher is worse) and stable-diffusion-v1-5/stable-diffusion-v1-5 (token agreement 100% → 97%: the share of token positions whose predicted token matches full precision's).

The tensors that lose most in their best format (their own error): layernorm bias in openai-community/gpt2 (fp8_e3m4, 34.5 dB), linear bias in stable-diffusion-v1-5/stable-diffusion-v1-5 (fp8_e2m5, 34.7 dB), linear output in stable-diffusion-v1-5/stable-diffusion-v1-5 (fp8_e3m4, 35.8 dB), groupnorm bias in stable-diffusion-v1-5/stable-diffusion-v1-5 (fp8_e2m5, 35.8 dB), add output in stable-diffusion-v1-5/stable-diffusion-v1-5 (fp8_e3m4, 36.2 dB), linear bias in google/vit-base-patch16-224 (fp8_e3m4, 36.5 dB), linear bias in openai-community/gpt2 (fp8_e2m5, 36.6 dB), conv2d bias in stable-diffusion-v1-5/stable-diffusion-v1-5 (fp8_e3m4, 36.6 dB), add output in google/vit-base-patch16-224 (fp8_e3m4, 36.6 dB) and add output in openai-community/gpt2 (fp8_e2m5, 36.7 dB).

Separately, the error accumulated along the data path (every tensor before a node quantized too): softmax outputs end furthest from full precision, jonatasgrosman/wav2vec2-large-xlsr-53-japanese keeping only 0.5 dB there. The outputs furthest from full precision in each model's best format set: softmax in jonatasgrosman/wav2vec2-large-xlsr-53-japanese (fp8_e3m4, 0.5 dB), bmm in jonatasgrosman/wav2vec2-large-xlsr-53-japanese (fp8_e3m4, 1.4 dB), linear in jonatasgrosman/wav2vec2-large-xlsr-53-japanese (fp8_e3m4, 1.7 dB), linear in mobilevit_s.cvnets_in1k (fp8_e2m5, 9.2 dB), gelu in jonatasgrosman/wav2vec2-large-xlsr-53-japanese (fp8_e3m4, 9.9 dB), silu in mobilevit_s.cvnets_in1k (fp8_e2m5, 10.5 dB), attention in mobilevit_s.cvnets_in1k (fp8_e2m5, 11.1 dB), linear in google/vit-base-patch16-224 (fp8_e3m4, 11.4 dB), mul in jonatasgrosman/wav2vec2-large-xlsr-53-japanese (fp8_e3m4, 11.4 dB) and layernorm in mobilevit_s.cvnets_in1k (fp8_e2m5, 11.5 dB).

Formats chosen (E = exponent bits, M = mantissa bits, u = unsigned): fp8_e2m5 2251 (59%), fp8_e3m4 929 (24%), fp8_e1m6 633 (17%); 0% of tensors use an unsigned format.

A wider format or a per-row choice would recover most where a tensor's own error in its format, times its data, is largest: silu output in stable-diffusion-v1-5/stable-diffusion-v1-5:vae (fp8_e2m5, 42.4 dB), conv2d weight in stable-diffusion-v1-5/stable-diffusion-v1-5:vae (fp8_e2m5, 42.7 dB) and conv2d bias in stable-diffusion-v1-5/stable-diffusion-v1-5:vae (fp8_e2m5, 43.2 dB).

body:
A kernel reads a tensor in the arrangement its writer stored it in; when the reader needs another arrangement, the reading kernel has to rearrange the data itself. This happens to 241 of 347 tensors passed between kernels (69%) in 5 models: 195 for attention heads split or merged, 27 for other reshapes, 16 for pixels reordered and 3 for image patches.

The reading operations are 135 operations (135 calls, 8.98% of all calls; 78 G MACs, 3.44% of all MACs). The most common causes (writer → reader): linear → attention (attention heads split or merged) 123, linear → bmm (attention heads split or merged) 72 and conv2d → add (pixels reordered) 16; most in stable-diffusion-v1-5/stable-diffusion-v1-5 (128), openai-community/gpt2 (36) and google/vit-base-patch16-224 (36).

Cost today: extra cycles not measured yet (no reading kernel has run); 0 links fail.
title: Layout conversions: 241 of 347 tensors between kernels are rearranged

body:
Activations such as exp, GELU and reciprocal go through a 256-entry lookup table (LUT), which limits their precision: 496 operations in 5 models (496 calls, 33% of all calls), most often silu (152), layernorm (119) and groupnorm (113). Their quantized accuracy: worst 10.5 dB SQNR over 496 measured operations.

Kernels per forward pass (host launches, one per planned kernel call): median 13, most 49 (stable-diffusion-v1-5/stable-diffusion-v1-5, 49 planned groups), over 5 models.

FP32 headroom (how far the largest value is from FP32 overflow, in powers of ten) is least at 35.0 powers of ten for add in openai-community/gpt2 (largest value 3.08e+03).

13 outputs in 1 model hold a value at the FP32 limit itself (mostly add (12) and select_where (1), e.g. an attention mask's fill value); they are counted apart from the headroom.

Instruction memory (IMEM, 1,024 words per bank) use: not measured yet (no kernel built).
title: Resource limits: 496 operations limited by the LUT and up to 49 kernel launches per pass

body: Across the surveyed models, the biggest measured IPU cost is layout conversion: 161 of 235 inter-kernel tensors (69%) must be rearranged by the reading kernel — mostly attention head splits/merges (123) — affecting 79 operations (8.8% of calls, 17% of MACs), though the cycle cost is not yet measured. Next is resource pressure from the 256-entry LUT, which handles 292 operations (32% of calls, e.g. silu, layernorm, groupnorm) at a worst 10.5 dB SQNR, plus up to 49 kernel launches per pass (median 31) and a minimum FP32 headroom of 35.4 powers of ten. Accuracy costs from NX8 formats come next: model outputs keep a median 24.7 dB SQNR (worst 12.7 dB), with 3 of 5 models losing prediction quality (e.g. GPT-2 perplexity 47 → 81.5, SD-VAE token agreement 100% → 68%), linear bias faring worst in its best format at 34.7 dB; along the data path, linear outputs accumulate the most error (worst 9.0 dB in ViT). The dominant format chosen is fp8_e2m5 (57%), with fp8_e3m4 at 26% and fp8_e1m6 at 18%. Not yet measured are MAC utilisation and IMEM usage, and no ISA gaps, workarounds, or what-if capability gaps affect the planned models.
